data.title: Scheduled Task Creation Unrestricted and Unmonitored
data.summary:
Scheduled tasks could be created locally and remotely on hosts across the estate, providing
execution, persistence and privilege escalation in a single mechanism, with no alerting on
task creation.
data.description:
Scheduled tasks are unusually valuable to an operator because one mechanism covers three
tactics: it executes code, it survives reboot, and a task configured to run as SYSTEM
escalates whoever can create it.

Remote creation extends this across the estate wherever administrative access is held, and
it is a well-worn lateral movement route that requires no additional tooling.

Task creation is a high-quality detection opportunity — the events are specific, and
legitimate creation outside deployment tooling is rare — but it is only useful if the
events are collected, which they frequently are not.
data.recommendation:
* Alert on scheduled task creation and modification, excluding the known deployment
  tooling rather than excluding the event.
* Restrict remote task creation to administrative tiers and management hosts.
* Review existing tasks for ones that run from user-writable paths or as SYSTEM without a
  recorded owner.
data.short_recommendation: Alert on task creation and restrict remote creation to management hosts.
